The perpetrator had recently been released from jail, he was imprisoned in 2015 following investigations for which the testimony of the victim was key. He had promised to retaliate. 1 fatality.

On 9 December 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of demonstrators, including students, members of unspecified political parties, civil society representatives, and members of the Transparency Venezuela movement, summoned by the Anti-Corruption Youth Network, gathered in protest against corruption, and to demand access to public information, accountability from the authorities, and additional civil society participation in political affairs.

On 11 December 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of residents of the La Isabelica neighborhood, in the Rafael Urdaneta parish, protested against piped drinking water outages going on for at least four days. The problems with the drinking water supply service began almost three years ago. They demand solutions from the authorities and the Hidrocentro water company.
On 12 December 2023, in Carabobo state (coded to Valencia), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, social security, and political participation.

On 19 December 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of demonstrators, including health workers, and representatives of the Carabobo state Board of Nursing, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and improvements in public transportation, access to medicines, and healthcare. They gathered outside the seat of the Carabobo state government, and then marched to the Carabobeno Health Institute Foundation (INSALUD) premises.

On 20 December 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of active and laid-off workers at the Diana food manufacturing company protested to demand their reinstatement in the company, the resumption of operations at the plant, and payment of owed stipends corresponding to benefits. They gathered outside company premises, where they met with some officials.

On 21 December 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of demonstrators, including workers at the state-owned Cardboard Corporation of Venezuela (CARTOVEN), and representatives of the Molino Valencia Production Council of Workers (CPTT), protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to vacation bonuses, Christmas Basket handouts, and presents for their children, as stipulated in their collective labor agreement. They gathered outside the company's premises in the Sur II Municipal Industrial Zone.

On 11 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including LGBTQ+ and human rights activists, protested to demand equal rights, and the publication in the Official Gazette of the law that will enable transgender, intersexual, and non-binary people to change their legal names at the National Electoral Council (CNE), the body in charge of managing the civil registry. They marched from the Vice President's Office to the CNE Office.

On 11 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including health workers at the Caracas University Hospital, and representatives of that hospital's workers' union, protested to demand justice for one of their colleagues, a nurse, that died the week prior after being refused medical attention at the Caracas University Hospital. The protesters, who blame the hospital director, claim that the woman was denied admittance to the emergency room due to medicine shortages, and lack of beds, and was told to seek medical attention elsewhere. She died while waiting in a car, outside the ER. The protest was staged by the Caracas University Hospital.

On 12 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including members of the Consensus Platform, and representatives of the Popular Vanguard political party, and the SITRASALUD health workers' union, protested to demand the publication of the 2024 Presidential Election calendar, and to call for the expedition of the electoral register registration procedures, and the voting process for Venezuelan nationals abroad. They gathered outside the National Electoral Council (CNE) Office, where they handed in a letter with their demands.
On 13 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, housing, political participation, and social security.

On 14 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including members of the Popular Front in Defense of Pay (FRENPODES), and other unionists, protested outside the Supreme Court of Justice (TSJ) to demand answers over an appeal filed five months prior regarding improvements in pay and working conditions.

On 18 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), approximately 30 demonstrators, including active and retired education sector workers, health workers, public administration workers, pensioners, and representatives of the Federation of Retired Workers of Caracas, protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to up to four months of food bonuses, and to call for the mediation of the Distrito Capital state governor.

On 18 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of relatives of 35 migrants that went missing in October 2023, in an area close to the San Andres Island (Colombia), after boarding a boat bound for Nicaragua, protested to demand action from the Venezuelan General Attorney, and the expedition of the investigation and the judicial process. They gathered outside the Public Ministry Office.

On 19 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including teachers, unionists, and civil society representatives, protested to demand the inclusion of additional funding within the 2024 National Budget, to guarantee pay rises for them, the renewal of their collective labor agreement, and the liberation of all political prisoners before Christmas. They gathered outside the National Assembly.

On 20 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of relatives of the six unionists sentenced to 16 years in prison in the PNB La Yaguara prison, under accusations of conspiracy, that had been liberated that day as part of the Barbados agreement between opposition parties and the regime, gathered to celebrate the release of the six prisoners, and to demand the immediate liberation of the remaining political prisoners in Venezuela. The demonstrators gathered outside the PNB La Yaguara prison.

On 22 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including health workers and representatives of the Caracas Association of Nurses, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, additional funding for hospitals, better medical attention for patients, and to call for the cessation of maltreatment and threats towards them at their workplace. They gathered outside the Public Ministry Office.

On 27 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of workers and representatives of the Union Coalition gathered to demand better pay and working conditions for Venezuelan workers, and announced further labor action for 2024. They gathered by the gates of the Tamanaco entrance to the Central Venezuela University (UCV) campus.

On 29 December 2023, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired state workers, and representatives of the SITRA-Ensenanza teachers' union, protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to two months of food and subsistence bonuses, which amount to roughly 80 USD per worker. They gathered in the Bolivar Square.

On 5 January 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including retired state workers, pensioners, teachers, and representatives of the SITRA-Ensenanza and the Distrito Capital SINVEMA-FVM teachers' unions, and the National Center for Retired Workers and Pensioners, protested to demand better pay, pensions, and working conditions, and payment of owed stipends corresponding to two months of food bonuses. They gathered outside the Public Ministry Office in Carabobo Park.

Around 14 December 2023 (as reported), in Punta Cardon (Falcon), a group of fishers protested to demand answers regarding the compensation promised to them by the state-owned PDVSA oil company for the numerous oil spills that have taken place in the Gulf of Coro during the past four years. These spills affect fisheries and the environment. They gathered in the Bolivar Square.

On 11 December 2023, in Punto Fijo (Falcon), a group of demonstrators, including residents and members of the Arab Muslim Community, marched in support of Palestine, and against the response of Israel to the attack from Hamas which they argue to be a massacre and a crime against humanity. They marched down the Bolivar Avenue to the Jose Leonardo Chirinos Square.

On 21 December 2023, in Tacuato (Falcon), a group of approximately 200 residents and fishers blocked the Troncal 4 road with sticks and debris in protest to demand compensation from the state-owned PDVSA oil company for the numerous oil spills that have taken place in the Gulf of Coro. These spills affect fisheries and the environment. The roadblock lasted almost the entire day. During the month prior, following a series of protests in the area, fishers from the Rio Seco and Punta Cardon villages (Falcon) received compensation pay-outs from PDVSA.

On 1 January 2024, in El Vinculo (Falcon), several members of the Los Betos Gang injured a woman with a machete, and partially looted her house. It is thought that the son of the victim had an unpaid debt with the suspects. The woman was taken to hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.

On 13 December 2023, in Coro (Falcon), a group of residents of the Antonio Jose de Sucre neighborhood blocked the Calle 4 Street, in the Cruz Verde sector, in protest against the collapse of the local sewage system that has led to stagnant water puddles in the area, and to demand improvements in street lighting and the paving of local roads. They claim that the problems with the sewage system affect at least 60 families. They demand solutions from the Hidrofalcon water company. PNB police officers were present but there was no intervention.

On 15 December 2023, in Coro (Falcon), a group of demonstrators, including residents and relatives of two women that died at the Alfredo Van Grieken Hospital over what they deem as medical malpractice, protested to demand justice for them. They gathered outside that hospital, in the El Tenis Avenue.

On 21 December 2023, in Coro (Falcon), a group of tipper lorry drivers gathered in the Jose Leonardo Chirinos Avenue in protest to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to asphalt and sand transportation services rendered to the Falcon state government. The protesters claim that after reporting the situation a few months back, they began to be excluded from new governmental construction management projects.

On 3 January 2024, in Boca de Aroa (Falcon), a group of residents blocked the Troncal 3 Moron - Coro road with branches and debris in protest over power outages going on for several days. GNB military and PNB police forces were present, but there was no intervention. The protest was lifted in the evening, following negotiations with Corpoelec power company officials.

On 26 December 2023, in Tucacas (Falcon), a group of inmates of the CICPC Police Tucacas prison set fire to part of their clothes to demonstrate over the cancellation of prison visits. The Tucacas fire department put out the fire. Several police bodies and GNB military forces were present, but there was no intervention. Some of the prisoners were injured during the fire, but the exact number is unknown. There were no fatalities.

On 3 January 2024, in Tucacas (Falcon), a group of residents of the Brisas del Mar neighborhood blocked the Troncal 3 Moron - Coro road in protest over power outages going on for several days. The protest was lifted in the evening, following negotiations with Corpoelec power company officials.

On 15 December 2023, in San Juan de los Morros (Guarico), a group of demonstrators, including relatives of political prisoners, and representatives of the National Conflict Committee of Workers in Struggle, gathered to demand the liberation of all political prisoners before Christmas.
On 20 December 2023, in La Guaira state (coded to La Guaira), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor and essential services.

On 18 December 2023, in Maiquetia (La Guaira), a group of laid-off workers at the Salva Foods food distributing company, and their lawyers, protested to demand payment of their dismissal pay-outs, owed since September 2021. According to them, at least 2,500 workers are affected by this situation. They gathered outside the labor courthouse.

On 11 December 2023, in Lara state (coded to Barquisimeto), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, housing, healthcare, water, justice, economic rights, political participation, and social security.

On 12 December 2023, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of residents of the El Cercado, Manuelita Saenz, and the El Carmen sectors, and representatives of the Manuelita Saenz Comunal Council, protested against piped drinking water outages going on for several months. They demand solutions from the authorities and the Hidrolara water company. The protesters gathered outside the Hidrolara office.

On 15 December 2023, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of demonstrators, including teachers, and representatives of the Lara state SINVEMA-FVM teachers' union, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, payment of owed stipends corresponding to bonuses, and against changes to their pay slips carried out by the administration, which have led hundreds of teachers to losing certain benefits and pay. They gathered outside the Office of the Lara state Comptroller General, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 26 December 2023, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of residents of the Concepcion parish protested over piped water outages going on for several months. According to them, this problem affects at least 1,800 families. They gathered outside the Hidrolara water company offices.

On 3 January 2024, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of recently laid-off workers at the Municipal Institute for Public Sanitation (IMAUBAR) protested to demand their reinstatement in the company, and payment of owed stipends. They gathered by the Labor Ministry Office.

On 27 December 2023, near San Pedro village (Lara), a group of residents of the Sicarigua sector blocked the Troncal 1 Lara - Trujillo Road with burning tires and debris to demonstrate over power outages going on for several months.

On 18 December 2023, in Hoyo de La Puerta (Miranda), CICPC and Baruta municipality police forces clashed with members of the El Santanita Gang, leaving three suspects dead, and an injured police officer, during several shootouts that broke out after a vehicle theft. The initial armed theft had taken place in the Autovia Regional del Centro Highway, and a police chase ensued. A clash broke out in Hoyo de La Puerta, a second one in the La Trinidad tunnel, and a third one in the Los Picapiedras sector. Three suspects were shot and killed, and a police officer was injured after being run over by the escaping gang members. The rest of the suspects fled. There is no further information at this point in time. 3 fatalities.

On 22 December 2023, in Caracas - Chacao (Miranda), a group of demonstrators, including Central University of Venezuela (UCV) students, and representatives of the Federation of UCV University Centers (FCU-UCV), protested to demand the immediate liberation of all political prisoners, including a UCV student arrested on 30 August 2023, and prosecuted under accusations of conspiracy. They gathered in the Juan Pablo II Square.

On 27 December 2023, in Caracas - Chacao (Miranda), a group of demonstrators, including retired Transport Ministry workers, and representatives of the National Federation of Retired Workers and Pensioners, protested to demand payment of owed bonuses, and observance of their collective labor agreement. They partially blocked the Francisco de Miranda Avenue. PNB police forces were present, but there was no intervention.

On 6 November 2023, in Caracas - El Hatillo (Miranda), several El Santanita gang members shot and killed a police officer, during an attack following an armed theft in a house in the Los Naranjos sector. It is thought that the officer had no relation with the assaulted residence, and that he was an undercover agent investigating some unspecified matter in the area. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 11 December 2023, in Miranda state (coded to Los Teques), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, housing, healthcare, water, justice, economic rights, political participation, and social security.

On 22 December 2023, in Los Teques (Miranda), a group of residents and merchants blocked the La Hoyada Avenue in protest over power outages going on for at least a day. The problems with the power service have extended for over six months, and affect businesses that operate in the La Hoyada Mall and its vicinity.

On 4 August 2023, in Paracotos (Miranda), five unidentified crime group suspects shot, stabbed, and killed, a rival gang member, in an attack over territorial disputes in the early hours of the day. The suspects entered their victim's house, dragged the man outside, shot him three times, and then finished him off with machetes they were carrying. They escaped through a forested area. Several months later, two of the perpetrators were arrested. 1 fatality.

On 27 December 2023, in Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), suspected members of the El Cheo Gang shot and killed three fellow gang members, in an attack during the evening over a settling of scores in the Valle Fresco sector, Filas de Mariche parish. According to witnesses, the perpetrators intercepted their victims and opened fire on them without any further interaction. Some reports claim that the victims were members of a rival criminal group instead, but this could not be confirmed. There is no further information at this point in time. 3 fatalities.

Around 1 January 2024 (as reported), in Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), a member of the Wilexis Gang was shot and killed, and his body found in the Jose Felix Ribas neighborhood, Petare parish. It is thought that the deceased had been intercepted by rival gang members in the early hours, during the New Year's celebrations, and shot dead. There is no further information on the identity of the perpetrators. 1 fatality.

On 15 December 2023, in Sucre municipality (coded to Turumo, Miranda), a group of demonstrators, relatives of victims of a multi-vehicle crash at KM 6 of the Troncal 9 Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho highway two days earlier, that resulted in at least 27 fatalities, protested to demand information about them and action from the authorities. They gathered in that highway, in an area close to the accident. Miranda state police forces were present and negotiated with the protesters; in the end they gave them a lift to the Bello Monte morgue.

On 11 December 2023, in Maturin (Monagas), a group of demonstrators, including workers at the Maturin municipality hall, and representatives of the Union of Public Workers at the Maturin Municipal Hall and Municipal Councils, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, payment of owed stipends, and the restoration of their medical insurance and burial plans.

On 14 December 2023, in La Asuncion (Nueva Esparta), a group of health workers protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to bonuses related to holiday, productivity, uniforms, and their Christmas pay-outs. They gathered outside the seat of the Nueva Esparta state government.

On 23 December 2023, in La Asuncion (Nueva Esparta), a group of residents of the Buenos Aires sector, and an elected municipal council member (COPEI), gathered in protest over water outages going on for at least 60 days, and to demand solutions from the Hidrocaribe water company.

On 23 September 2023, in Guanare (Portuguesa), an unidentified crime group suspect on a motorcycle shot and killed a woman, in a drive-by shooting in the El Libertador neighborhood. The victim was intercepted by the perpetrator as she was coming out of her house to work, and was shot at least 18 times. The shooter was arrested several weeks after. It was later established that this contract killing had been ordered by the leader of an Ecuadorian drug-trafficking gang, who had a dispute with the victim's son over a Venezuelan woman. For this reason the son had already fled to Peru and the woman to Spain. 1 fatality.

Around 25 December 2023 (as reported), in Mete Miedo (Trujillo), Trujillo state police forces shot and killed a member of the El Nichito Gang, during an armed confrontation with several of them. The suspects resisted authority and a shootout ensued. One of them was injured in the gunfire and pronounced dead in hospital. The rest of the shooters escaped. The deceased was linked to unspecified crimes. Police collected a gun. 1 fatality.

On 8 December 2023, in Maracaibo (Zulia), a group of demonstrators, including relatives of political prisoners, civil society representatives, university students, human rights activists, and members of the PJ political party, protested to demand the liberation of all political prisoners before Christmas, and the closing down of what they deem as torture centers. They gathered by the Basilica San Juan de Dios temple.

On 13 December 2023, in Maracaibo (Zulia), a group of demonstrators, including health workers, and representatives of the Board of Nursing, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and an additional Christmas bonus. They gathered outside the Health Ministry Office in the Bella Vista Avenue, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 15 December 2023, in Maracaibo (Zulia), approximately 50 demonstrators, including oil sector workers at the state-owned PDVSA oil company, and representatives of the Unitary Platform of Oil and Gas Sector Workers (FUTPV), marched in support of the government's plans regarding Venezuela's ongoing international territorial dispute over the Esequibo territories currently belonging to Guyana. They marched down the La Limpia Avenue to the PDVSA office.

Around 3 January 2024 (as reported), in Maracaibo (Zulia), a vigilante group of residents of the Teotiste de Gallegos neighborhood, Coquivacoa parish, attempted to lynch a man who they accused of sexually abusing a girl. Police arrived at the scene and found the man tied up and bruised. The suspect was arrested and taken to hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.

On 4 January 2024, in Maracaibo (Zulia), several members of rival unidentified criminal groups exchanged gunfire, during an armed clash in the Santa Rosa de Agua neighborhood, Coquivacoa parish. A civilian woman who was in the company of her daughter was injured by a stray bullet and taken to hospital for treatment. The shooters escaped. There is no further information at this point in time. There were no fatalities.

On 22 December 2023, in San Francisco (Zulia), a group of fishers from the El Bajo and San Luis communities protested to demand payment for their labor in cleaning up a recent oil spill in Lake Maracaibo. They gathered outside the AMPSA C.A company premises.

Property destruction: Around 4 January 2024 (as reported), in San Francisco (Zulia), two members of the Ye Nava Gang opened fire on a house in an extortion-related attack in the Negro Primero neighborhood. The owner of the house and his relatives had received death threats in the days prior, and had refused to pay a 500 USD fee. The attack caused some property damage on the residence and the victims' private vehicle. Before escaping, the suspects left behind an extortion letter signed by the Ye Nava Gang, demanding payment of the 500 USD within the following 24 hours. Both perpetrators were arrested hours later, one of them was an adolescent boy.
On 8 January 2024, in Amazonas state (coded to Puerto Ayacucho), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.
On 8 January 2024, in Anzoategui state (coded to Barcelona), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.
On 8 January 2024, in Aragua state (coded to Maracay), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.

On 9 January 2024, in Maracay (Aragua), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired teachers, pensioners, and representatives of the Civil Association of Retired Teachers and Pensioners, protested to demand better pay, pensions, and living conditions, the renewal of their collective labor agreement, better medical attention, and payment of owed pensions for 20,000 pensioners living abroad that had these payments terminated in 2015. They gathered in the Bicentenaria Square. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
On 11 January 2024, in Maracay (Aragua), a group of teachers of the Joaquin Avellaneda School protested to demand additional security in the area after several thefts.
On 8 January 2024, in Barinas state (coded to Barinas), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.

On 9 January 2024, in Barinas (Barinas), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired teachers, other university workers, and unionists of the Los Llanos Ezequiel Zamora University (UNELLEZ), protested to demand better pay and working conditions, the repeal of the National Budget Office (ONAPRE) instruction, and the renewal of their collective labor agreement. They gathered in Punto Fresco roundabout. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
On 10 January 2024, in Barinas state (coded to Barinas), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, land, social security, and water.

On 6 January 2024, in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar), four unidentified crime group suspects abducted a merchant, and member of the VP political party, in the vicinity of the Atlantico Avenue. Due to the heightened pressure of the security forces, the man was liberated by his captors the day after in the vicinity of the Sidor overpass. The identity or motivations of the kidnappers is unknown.

On 9 January 2024, in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired health workers, teachers, and workers at companies belonging to the state-owned Venezuelan Corporation of Guayana (CVG), and representatives of the Bolivar state School of Nursing Professionals, the School of Teaching Professionals, the ITG workers' union, and the National Front of the Working Class Struggle (FNLCT), protested to demand better pay and working conditions, the renewal of their collective labor agreements, improvements in the medical infrastructure, trade union autonomy, the restoration of their medical insurance and burial plans (HCM), and the liberation of all the unionists imprisoned while defending their labor rights. They gathered in the CVG Monument Square. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

On 10 January 2024, in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar), a group of retired workers at companies belonging to the state-owned Venezuelan Corporation of Guayana (CVG), pensioners, and representatives of the Bolivar state Federation of Associations of Retired Workers and Pensioners (FEDAJUPEBOL), and the CVG Carbonorca workers' union, gathered outside the CVG headquarters to demand payment of owed stipends, observance of their collective labor agreements, the restoration of their medical insurance and burial plans (HCM), and better medical attention.
On 8 January 2024, in Bolivar state (coded to Ciudad Bolivar), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.

On 9 January 2024, in Ciudad Bolivar (Bolivar), a group of demonstrators, including state workers, and supporters of the Popular Will (VP) political party, marched in protest to demand better pay and working conditions. They marched from the Public Ministry Office, where they handed in a letter with their demands, to the Ombudsman Office. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

On 6 January 2024, in Mariara (Carabobo), suspected members of the Los Guaricheros Gang shot and killed a man, in an attack occurred in the morning. The killing is thought to be a settling of scores. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 10 January 2024, in El Charal (Carabobo), CICPC police forces shot and killed the leader of the El Culita Gang during an armed clash. The suspect resisted authority, initiated the shooting, was injured in the gunfire, and pronounced dead in hospital. He was linked to homicides, extortion threats, and thefts. Police collected a gun. 1 fatality.

On 8 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired teachers, and representatives of the Carabobo state SINVEMA-FVM teachers' union, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, improvements in the educational infrastructure, and the restoration of their medical insurance and burial plans (HCM). They gathered in the Bolivar Avenue and then marched to the Education Secretary Office, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 8 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group workers at the state-owned Cardboard Corporation of Venezuela (CARTOVEN) protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to three vacation bonuses, Christmas Basket handouts, food tickets, and a week of pay. They gathered outside the company's premises in the Sur II Municipal Industrial Zone.

On 9 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), for the second consecutive day, a group of demonstrators, including active and retired state workers, teachers, representatives of the SITRA-Ensenanza and the SUMA Carabobo teachers' unions, the National Front of the Working Class Struggle (FNLCT), and the CUTEC and the FETRACARABOBO workers' unions, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, the renewal of their collective labor agreements, and the repeal of the National Budget Office (ONAPRE) instruction. They gathered in the La Candelaria parish, and then marched to the intersection of the Lara and the Las Ferias avenues. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

On 9 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of licensed merchants of the Los Guajiros Market protested to demand the relocation of the informal sellers that work in the area. According to them, these informal sellers block the access of customers to their shops, affecting the livelihoods of 3,000 merchants. They gathered outside the Valencia townhall, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 10 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), a group of residents of the El Trigal Sur neighborhood protested over water outages going on for at least six weeks, and to demand action from the Hidrocentro water company. They gathered in the vicinity of the residence of the Carabobo state governor.

On 11 January 2024, in Valencia (Carabobo), Carabobo state police forces shot and killed an unidentified crime group suspect, during an armed clash in the early hours in the Bicentenario sector, Negro Primero neighborhood. The deceased was thought to be one of the perpetrators of the theft-related killing of a public prosecutor in August 2023. Police collected a gun. 1 fatality.

On 9 January 2024, in San Carlos (Cojedes), a group of demonstrators, including teachers and health workers, marched in protest to demand better pay and working conditions. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

On 9 January 2024, in Tucupita (Delta Amacuro), a group of teachers, summoned by the Delta Amacuro state School of Teaching Professionals, protested to demand better pay, pensions and working conditions, and the renewal of their collective labor agreement. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
On 8 January 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.

On 9 January 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), hundreds of demonstrators, including active and retired state workers, pensioners, school teachers, health workers, Caracas Underground Tube workers, representatives of the Distrito Capital School of Nursing Professionals, the SITRA-Ensenanza teachers' union, and the Federation of Retired Education Sector Workers and Pensioners, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and the renewal of their collective labor agreement. They gathered outside the Public Ministry Office, by Carabobo Park. Elsewhere, a group of active and retired workers at the Central University of Venezuela (UCV), pensioners, and representatives of the National Union Coalition, protested with similar demands by the gates of the Tamanaco entrance to the UCV campus, and then marched to Venezuela Square. These were two of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

On 9 January 2024, in Punto Fijo (Falcon), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired state workers, school and Zulia University teachers, oil sector workers, health workers, representatives of the Falcon state SITRA-Ensenanza teachers' union, the Retired Oil Sector Workers' Association (AJIP), and other unionists, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and payment of owed stipends. They gathered in the Jose Leonardo Chirinos Square. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
On 8 January 2024, in Falcon state (coded to Coro), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to labor, justice, education, the environment, and healthcare.

On 9 January 2024, in Coro (Falcon), a group of demonstrators, including teachers, other active and retired state workers, pensioners, and representatives of the Intergremial trade union coalition, protested to demand better pay and working conditions. They gathered in the Sucre Square. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
On 12 January 2024, in Falcon state (coded to Coro), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, labor, healthcare, and education.

On 8 January 2024, in San Juan de los Morros (Guarico), a group of demonstrators, including teachers, and representatives of the Teachers' Union Coalition, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and the renewal of their collective labor agreement. They marched to the Education Zone Office.

On 9 January 2024, in San Juan de los Morros (Guarico), dozens of demonstrators, including active state workers, and representatives of the School of Nursing Professionals, protested to demand better pay, pensions, and working conditions, the renewal of their collective labor agreements, and improvements in healthcare. In Venezuela Square, a group of suspected colectivo and PSUV members that were on their way to join a pro-government march that took place later (coded separately), attempted to pass through the anti-government group that was blocking the streets, leading to a violent clash between the groups that left a small unspecified number of casualties on both sides. A journalist covering the event was slightly injured and had her camera stolen, but it was found shortly after. A small group of security forces were present and attempted to mediate and separate both groups. This demonstration was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations held on International Workers' Day.

On 1 May 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a very large group of demonstrators, including state workers, President Nicolas Maduro, the PSUV vice-president, the Miranda state and the Distrito Capital governors (PSUV), other government officials, and PSUV supporters, marched in support of the government and their labor rights, and against the international sanctions imposed on the country. On 15 January 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, a group of teachers protested to demand the increase in their salaries, the dollarization of their salaries, better working conditions, and better infrastructure within schools. The protest took place within the framework of a national protest.

On 12 February 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, residents from the Alberto Adriani municipality protested for more than seven hours to demand basic services such as potable water, electric power, gasoline, domestic gas, and telecommunications.

On 19 February 2020, in El Vigia, Alberto Adriani municipality, Merida state, protesters closed a road to demand electric power in the city. Protesters informed that they have been without electric power since February 14.
On 28 April 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, people and public transport drivers protested to demand public services.
On 8 May 2020, near the Simon Rodriguez University in El Vigia, Merida state, residents blocked a road to protest against the continuous electric shutdowns.
On 8 May 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, a group of workers from the milk company, Industria Lactea Venezolana C.A (Indulac), protested to demand better salaries and working conditions.

On 12 June 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, a group of citizens, who are in a hotel while they are completing the quarantine due to the coronavirus outbreak, protested due to the situation they are living inside the hotel. After 30 days, protesters are demanding the results of the test to find out if they have the coronavirus or not.

On 9 May 2020, in El Vigia (Merida), a violent demonstration was staged by residents of the city to reject the rationing of electricity. A supermarket was looted, the town hall was attacked, and tires were burnt.
On 11 August 2020, El Vigia, Merida state, a group of people blocked a highway to demand the distribution of domestic gas. Protesters informed that they have not received gas in four months.

On 5 October 2020, in El Vigia, Merida state, CICPC officers beat a group of prisoners with pipes and boards, in addition to torturing them. People that live in the area informed that the screams of prisoners were heard in the sector. No injuries or fatalities reported.

Around 10 October 2020 (between 5 October - 13 October), in Alberto Adriani municipality (Merida state), citizens demonstrated to reject the lack of basic public services and petrol. The source reported that in some cases demonstrators built barricades and set tires on fire during the events.

On 21 October 2020, in Alberto Adriani municipality (Merida state), teachers took to the streets to protest against President Maduro (PSUV) and to decry the payment of extremely low bonuses. Protesters demanded major economic reforms in the public sector, including increased salaries, social security, and better working conditions. Teachers also called for authorities to stop harassing and threatening them for protesting. The protest took place as part of the second nationwide protest called by teachers. Some other protests took place across the state that day.

On 10 December 2020, in El Vigia (Merida state), a protest was held to demand the release of political prisoners of Nicolas Maduro's regime and to ensure political freedom in the country. The protest took place in the context of the 72nd anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Venezuela.

On 15 January 2021, in El Vigia (Merida state), teachers took to the streets to demand higher salaries, better working conditions, and the implementation of benefits and bonuses, among other things. The event took place in the context of a nationwide protest to commemorate Teachers Day and to decry the socio-economic crisis that is afflicting the country.

No injuries or fatalities occurred.

On 22 April 2021, in El Vigia (Merida state), health workers staged a protest outside the Tipo II Hospital to decry the lack of petrol for the past month at the health establishment. Protesters reported the situation is severely affecting patients and workers, with some of the latter having to pay for gasoline in order to use the only ambulance available at the center.

On 12 May 2021, in El Vigia (Merida state), health workers took to the streets of the city in a protest to demand the effective provision of the coronavirus vaccine, protective gear at health centers, and higher salaries, among other things. Protesters reported their dire living conditions as a result of low wages and lack of working benefits. The event took place as part of a nationwide protest to commemorate International Nurses Day.

On 11 April 2024, in Quibor (Lara), CICPC police forces shot and killed an unidentified crime group suspect, during an armed clash in the Bolivar neighborhood. The suspect was being sought for homicide, and was linked to other several unspecified crimes. However, the family of the victim claims that the man had been extorted by the CICPC police officers for an extended period of time, that every time there was a crime in the area they would go to him to demand money to leave him out of trouble, and that he was unarmed at the time of his killing. 1 fatality.

On 1 May 2024, in Pedro Camejo municipality (coded to San Juan de Payara, Apure), military air forces shot down two aircraft thought to belong to unidentified armed groups linked to drug and arms trafficking. The aircraft had entered Venezuelan airspace at different times and locations, had no flight plans, were flying at low altitude, and had their radios and transponders switched off. Casualties unknown.

On 5 October 2021, in Carupano (Sucre), approximately 100 fishers blocked the Carupano-Cumana national highway to protest a lack of gasoline at three local ports. Demonstrators stated they are unable to work due to the fuel shortage, and blame the Ministry of Energy and the state-owned PDVSA oil company for the disruption.

On 2 December 2021, in Carupano (Sucre), workers and retirees of the state-owned CANTV telecom company protested to demand better salaries, healthcare, and a new collective bargaining agreement. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration against CANTV.

On 9 March 2022, in Carupano (Sucre), some 300 retirees protested in front of the social security office to demand higher pensions. The demonstration was part of a nationwide protest demanding better treatment of the nation's retirees and elderly.
On 4 November 2022, in Carupano (Sucre), workers from Sucregas protested to demand payment of owed stipends after years of delay. The protesters demonstrated outside the company's premises.
On 24 November 2022, in Carupano (Sucre), teachers and other workers protested to demand higher salaries in accordance with the rising cost of living. The protest took place in the Colon square.

On 26 July 2022, in Bermudez municipality (coded to Carupano, Sucre), police officers shot and killed a Los Guacharacos gang member, during an armed confrontation in a rural area in the La Cumbre de Maturincito sector. The suspect resisted arrest and opened fire on the officers. He was injured and taken to hospital, where he died. Residents agree that the victim was a criminal, but claim he was unarmed. Police collected a shotgun. 1 fatality.
Around 11 July 2020, in Ocumare del Tuy, Miranda state, two men were killed by members of the El Puti gang, in the San Juan de Soapire sector. The motive of the attack is unknown. 2 fatalities.

On 17 November 2020, in Carupano, Sucre, an off-duty police officer of CICPC was shot and killed by at least three armed assailants in a drive-by shooting. The suspects threw a grenade at him and the motivation of the crime is unknown.

Around 23 October 2019 (as reported), in Santa Lucia (Miranda), three people were killed and their bodies were found decapitated and burned in Casarapa de La Ceiba de Soapire sector. Authorities claim that El Puti gang and El Enyer gang are behind this killing and that the victims might be El Nino Gang members, who operate alongside Los Vizcainos gang. 3 fatalities.

On 12 January 2020, in Carupano (Sucre), a man was shot and killed and a woman was injured in the foot by an unidentified man who arrived on a motorcycle with his accomplice, got off the vehicle and started firing shots in Parque Miranda sector. Both perpetrators fled. Authorities claim it is a settling of scores case. 1 fatality.

On 8 February 2020, in an area between San Jose and Carupano town, Bermudez municipality (Sucre), unidentified armed individuals intercepted a car in La Curva del Guardia sector and shot and killed two men who were inside the vehicle. The motive is unknown. 2 fatalities.

Around 13 February 2020 (as reported), near Carupano town, Bermudez municipality (Sucre), a clash took place between CICPC police forces and two unidentified armed individuals in the Brisas del Carmen sector. One of them was killed in the clash and the other was arrested. 1 fatality.
On 27 February 2020, in Playa Grande (Sucre), a man was killed in a drive-by shooting by two men on a motorbike. The attack was motivated by a settlement of scores. 1 fatality.

On 1 June 2020, in Carupano (Sucre), two armed men on a motorcycle shot and killed a former police officer in Victoria street when he was about to leave his business. The victim was inside his vehicle at the moment of the attack. 1 fatality.
On 18 June 2020, near Carupano, Bermudez (Sucre), two armed men killed a truck driver in a drive-by shooting in Canchunchu community, 19 de Abril sector. 1 fatality.

On 20 January 2023, in Carupano (Sucre), workers of the Santos Anibal Dominicci Hospital protested over pay and other labor related demands.

On 26 January 2023, in Carupano (Sucre), residents of the 6 de Marzo neighborhood protested after 12 days of power outages. The demonstrators claim that there are approximately 100 affected households.

On 30 January 2023, in Carupano (Sucre), a group of teachers protested over pay and other labor demands. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day, on the fourth consecutive week of protests.

On 1 May 2023, in Carupano (Sucre), a group of state workers protested to demand better pay and working conditions. The protesters gathered in the Simon Bolivar Square, and then marched around town. Around 21 May 2023 (as reported), in Carupano (Sucre), a group of residents of the Las Azucenas neighborhood blocked the Troncal 9 road in protest over the power fluctuations and outages they suffer. On 12 September 2023, in Carupano (Sucre), residents of the La Ensenada and the Las Azucenas neighborhoods staged two separate demonstrations in protest over water outages going on for at least four months, and against the poor state of essential services in the area. That week, the Bermudez municipality mayor (PSUV) declared a local state of emergency due to the prolonged water outages.

On 12 September 2023, in Pozo Colorado (Sucre), for the second consecutive day, a group of approximately 70 residents of the La Cachapera sector continued blocking the Troncal 9 road in protest over power outages going on for several days due to the breakdown of an electric transformer, and problems with water supply. That week, the Bermudez municipality mayor (PSUV) declared a local state of emergency due to the prolonged water outages.

On 13 September 2023, in Pozo Colorado (Sucre), for the third consecutive day, a group of approximately 70 residents of the La Cachapera sector continued blocking the Troncal 9 road in protest over power outages going on for several days due to the breakdown of an electric transformer, and problems with water supply. That week, the Bermudez municipality mayor (PSUV) declared a local state of emergency due to the prolonged water outages. The roadblock was lifted that evening, following the arrival of a new electric transformer.

On 9 January 2024, in Carupano (Sucre), a group of demonstrators, including teachers and other state workers protested to demand better pay and working conditions. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.

This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day, coinciding with the Venezuelan Teachers' Day.

On 1 February 2024, in Carupano (Sucre), a group of workers at the SucreGas gas company in the Carupano 1 and 2 plants staged a walkout in protest to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to monthly compensation bonuses of 70 USD per employee, and better pay and working conditions. One of the shooters was injured in the gunfire and pronounced dead in hospital; it is suspected that the rest managed to escape. They marched from the CVG headquarters to the Palace of Justice, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 7 May 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of workers at the Central University of Venezuela (UCV), and members of the UCV Workers' Union, blocked the access road to the UCV campus at the Tamanaco Gate in protest to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to their medical insurance, maternity and burial plans (HCM), and better pay and working conditions.

On 10 May 2024, in Punto Fijo (Falcon), a group of relatives and colleagues of a Corpoelec power company worker who suffered burns on 35% of his body as a result of an electrical shock, and members of the Falcon state power workers' union, gathered to demand his transfer to a specialized hospital to treat his wounds. They gathered outside the Dr. Rafael Calles Sierra Hospital, where he was currently being treated.

On 9 May 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including university teachers and other workers, and representatives of the Simon Rodriguez University and the FENASOESV workers' unions, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and payment of owed stipends and benefits. They gathered outside the University Sector Planning Office (OPSU), where some of them met with officials.

On 6 May 2024, in El Tocuyo (Lara), a group of demonstrators, including psychologists, teachers at the UPTAEB University, work colleagues, members of the United for Orleana movement, friends, and relatives of a woman killed on 30 April by her boyfriend, in a suspected femicide, marched to pay tribute to her, and to demand justice, and the imposition of the maximum sentence for the culprit. On 2 July 2024, in San Felipe (Yaracuy), a group of residents of the La Cuchilla and the El Trompillo neighborhoods blocked the Intercomunal San Felipe El Fuerte Avenue in protest over piped water outages going on for at least 15 days. Police forces were present but there was no intervention. The protesters managed to speak with workers at the San Felipe town hall, who promised to send them a tanker truck with water.
On 3 July 2024, in Bachaquero (Zulia), a group of residents of the 23 de Enero sector blocked the San Pedro - Lagunillas road in protest over ongoing power outages.

On 3 July 2024, in Barcelona (Anzoategui), a group of residents of the La Ponderosa neighborhood partially blocked the Troncal 9 Jose Antonio Anzoategui Highway in protest to demand improvements in the power grid after a month of power cuts and fluctuations due to the breakdown of electric transformers. At least 20 families are affected by this situation; local authorities argue that they do not have any spare electric transformers, but that they are working to provide a solution. The roadblock lasted four hours, causing significant traffic congestion.

On 2 July 2024, in Amazonas state (coded to Puerto Ayacucho), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to justice, free speech, labor, education, social security, petrol, and politics.

On 2 July 2024, in Bolivar state (coded to Ciudad Bolivar), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to justice, free speech, labor, education, social security, petrol, and politics.

On 2 July 2024, in Lara state (coded to Barquisimeto), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to justice, free speech, labor, education, social security, petrol, and politics.

On 23 June 2024, in Ocumare de la Costa (Aragua), two suspected members of the El Tren de Aragua gang shot and killed a man, a judge who had served in the National Assembly, and who had been the Carabobo and La Guaira states comptroller, in an attack in the La Boca sector during the San Juan Bautista festivities. The killing took place in the street, while the victim was in the company of his family and friends. Four other people were injured in the gunfire. The attackers escaped in a motorcycle and then a speedboat. It was later established that the killing had been ordered by the leader of the gang, and that the perpetrators had been paid 1200 USD for it. Both perpetrators would be arrested two weeks later, and a third suspect shot and killed by the security forces during the same operation (coded separately). 1 fatality.

On 30 April 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), thousands of high-school and university students belonging to several universities, including the Bolivarian University (UBV), the UNETI, the Simon Rodriguez University, and the UNEFA University, and a National Assembly member (PSUV), marched in support of Palestine, and called for an end of what they deem is a genocide being perpetrated by Israel. The Palestinian Ambassador for Venezuela was also present. They marched from the UBV campus to the National Assembly.

On 12 July 2024, in Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), a group of residents and animal rights activists protested outside the Farmatodo La Carlota Pharmacy to demand information on the whereabouts of a stray dog that used to live in the nearby Farmatodo Los Dos Caminos Pharmacy, and that went missing several weeks prior.

Around 12 July 2024 (as reported), near La Victoria city (Aragua), military forces exchanged shots with two members of the Luis Manilla gang, injuring one, in an armed clash during a security operation to liberate an adolescent boy who had been abducted for a 20,000 USD ransom the day before (coded separately). The captive was liberated safely, and both suspects were arrested. Military forces collected a gun, and seized a vehicle. There is no further information at this point in time. There were no fatalities.

On 11 July 2024, in Barquisimeto (Lara), for the second consecutive day, a small group of property owners of unfinished flats in the area known as Triangulo del Este protested to demand answers from the authorities and a construction company regarding the stoppage of the construction works of five apartment blocks, and to be allowed to occupy their flats despite these lacking essential services such as piped water and power. The owners argue that they are victims of fraud. The protesters gathered by the Plaza Mayor apartment block, in the Paseo Juan Guillermo Iribarren Avenue.

On 11 July 2024, in La Victoria (Aragua), several members of the Luis Manilla gang abducted an adolescent boy in the La Mora sector, and demanded a 20,000 USD ransom for his liberation. Around a day later, military forces clashed with the kidnappers, thwarting the exchange for ransom, and liberating the captive safely (coded separately).

On 10 July 2024, in Punto Fijo (Falcon), a group of relatives of a kitesurf instructor that was shot and killed in unclear circumstances by another man on November 2023, protested to demand justice for him, the expedition of the judicial process, and to call for an end of the privileges, that according to them, the culprit receives while awaiting trial in prison. The court hearing scheduled for that day was postponed due to judge illness.

On 10 July 2024, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of property owners of unfinished flats in the area known as Triangulo del Este, and members of the I Want My Property Civil Association protested to demand answers from the authorities and a construction company regarding the stoppage of the construction works of five apartment blocks. Some of the owners demanded to be allowed to occupy their flats despite these lacking essential services such as piped water and power. The owners argue that they are victims of fraud. The protesters gathered by the Plaza Mayor and the Paseo de la Castellana apartment blocks, in the Paseo Juan Guillermo Iribarren Avenue.

On 9 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including active and retired workers at the Simon Rodriguez Experimental University (UNESR), and members of the National Federation of University Workers' Unions (FENASOESV), and the Simon Rodriguez University Workers' Union, protested to demand payment of owed stipends corresponding to the purchase of uniforms, their retirement status, and interests accrued by their pension fund. In some cases these delays have extended for over eight years. They gathered outside the University Sector Planning Office (OPSU), where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 8 July 2024, in Curaima (Bolivar), a group of residents and a municipal council official protested to demand the authorities assistance and the repair of the Puchima Bridge, which collapsed due to heavy rain in 2022. According to them, due to the inaction from local authorities, they had to resort to building a makeshift walkway with their own means, only for it to be washed away by torrential rain the day prior to the demonstration. Because of these circumstances they are now completely cut-off from the rest of the country.

On 8 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of cancer patients protested to demand the provision of a drug required for their cancer treatments at subsidized prices. According to them, the IVSS Alto Costo Social Security pharmacies have not been handing out this medicine in over three months, but there are other private pharmacies that do sell this product at unaffordable prices. They argue that several patients have died during the interlude. They gathered outside the IVSS Social Security main office, where they managed to speak with the National Director of Pharmacotherapeutics, who claimed that the medicines are blocked for unclear reasons at the La Guaira Port.

Around 8 July 2024 (as reported), in Valencia (Carabobo), a man was shot and killed, and his body found with at least 15 gunshot wounds by the Villa Real CDI health center. The victim had been taken by force the night before by several suspected members of the Luis El Feo gang. It is suspected that his killing happened in retaliation for another unspecified killing perpetrated by the deceased. It is unknown whether he was affiliated to a criminal group. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 8 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including workers at the Caracas Townhall, and members of the Municipal Government Workers' Union (SUOMGIA), protested in support of a colleague and unionist, who was suspended without pay, and forced into retirement in unclear circumstances by the Human Resources Department of the Caracas Townhall. They argue that this decision was arbitrary, and poses a violation to her human and labor rights. They gathered outside the townhall.

On 8 July 2024, in Anzoategui state (coded to Barcelona), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to water, housing, labor, food, political participation, healthcare, and children's rights.

On 8 July 2024, in Miranda state (coded to Los Teques), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to water, housing, labor, food, political participation, healthcare, and children's rights.

On 8 July 2024, in Nueva Esparta state (coded to Porlamar), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to water, housing, labor, food, political participation, healthcare, and children's rights.

On 8 July 2024, in Sucre state (coded to Cumana), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to water, housing, labor, food, political participation, healthcare, and children's rights.

On 8 July 2024, in San Francisco de Yare (Miranda), several members of the Carlos Capa gang opened fire on two brothers travelling in a vehicle, injuring one in the shoulder, after luring them with a fake Facebook Marketplace car for sale advertisement, in an attack in the La Pollera sector of the Salamanca neighborhood. The victims had travelled all the way from Tachira state. Upon arriving in the aforementioned sector, they spotted the armed group of men, realized it was a trap, and sped-off, at which point the suspects opened fire. They suffered a traffic accident during their escape, but were brought to safety by other drivers, and taken to hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.

On 7 July 2024, between Caracas - Chacao and Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), thousands of demonstrators, including LGBTQ+ and human rights activists, unspecified diplomatic figures, and members of NGOs, marched to demand equal rights, same-sex marriage, and respect for their identity, and against any form of discrimination. The march began in the Francisco de Miranda Avenue, by the Cristal Park.

On 7 July 2024, in Cumanacoa (Sucre), for the third consecutive day, a group of residents protested over the government's response to the emergency caused by Hurricane Beryl, which left at least three people dead, extensive property damage, and thousands without shelter due to the overflowing of the Manzanares River. On that day, the demonstrators blocked the village's main avenue with branches, debris, pots, damaged house appliances and mattresses. They demanded government attention, and the provision of drinking water, food, and shelter.

Around 7 July 2024 (as reported), near Maracay city (Aragua), CICPC police forces shot and killed a suspected member of the El Tren de Aragua gang, and arrested two others, during an armed confrontation. The three of them were being sought for their participation in the killing of the former Carabobo and La Guaira states comptroller, which took place on 23 June (coded separately). During the security operation the police forces seized five vehicles, and collected a gun. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 6 July 2024, in Cumanacoa (Sucre), for the second consecutive day, a group of residents protested over the government's response to the emergency caused by Hurricane Beryl, which left at least three people dead, extensive property damage, and thousands without shelter due to the overflowing of the Manzanares River. On that day, the demonstrators also protested against the visit of the Sucre state governor (PSUV), who was forced to leave the area. Once again, they demanded government attention, and the provision of drinking water, food, and shelter. Police and military forces were present, but there was no intervention.

On 5 July 2024, in Camuri Grande (La Guaira), a group of residents blocked a local bridge in protest over ongoing power outages and fluctuations. According to them, these fluctuations damage their house appliances and negatively impact their living conditions.

On 5 July 2024, in Cumanacoa (Sucre), a group of residents of the San Baltazar neighborhood blocked a street in protest over the government's response to the emergency caused by Hurricane Beryl, which left at least three people dead, extensive property damage, and thousands without shelter due to the overflowing of the Manzanares River. They demanded the provision of drinking water, food, and shelter. Police and military forces were present, but there was no intervention.

Property destruction: On 18 July 2024, in Barquisimeto (Lara), unidentified people vandalized the vehicles of the electoral convoy of former Come Venezuela (VV) presidential candidate, Maria Corina Machado, in the early hours, during her visit in Lara state in support of presidential candidate Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia (MUD/PUEDE). It is suspected that the damage to the vehicles was caused by members of colectivos, or PSUV supporters, although this could not be confirmed. The vandalizing included spraying paint on the vehicles, the writing of a message that read 'no to the blockade', and the disabling of the vehicles' brakes.

Around 18 July 2024 (as reported), in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar), a group of demonstrators, including retired workers at companies belonging to the Venezuelan Corporation of Guayana (CVG), pensioners, teachers at the National Experimental University of Guayana (UNEG), and members of the APUNEG teachers' union, protested to demand better pensions, living conditions, access to medicines, observance of their collective labor agreements, and respect. Likewise, they called for a political change in the country in the upcoming presidential election.

On 18 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of demonstrators, including human rights activists, relatives of political prisoners, and representatives of the Provea, the Justice, Union, and Forgiveness (Justicia, Encuentro y Perdon), and the Voices of Memories (Voces de Memorias) NGOs, protested to demand the government and the judiciary to stop using the judiciary system, and certain laws, as a mechanism of political repression and criminalization. More specifically, they rejected the indiscriminate use of two laws: the Law Against Organized Crime and Financing of Terrorism (LODOFAT), and the Law Against Hate, for Peaceful Coexistence and Tolerance. Likewise, they demanded better living conditions for the around 300 political prisoners that they claim to be imprisoned in Venezuela, and the cessation of torture. They gathered outside the Public Ministry Office, where they handed in a letter with their demands.

On 17 July 2024, in Maracay (Aragua), three armed unidentified crime group suspects abducted a man from a liquor store, after arriving in two vehicles and robbing everybody inside. PNB police forces liberated the captive approximately two days later, during a special security operation in the Fundocoropo neighborhood. There is no further information on the identity or motive of the perpetrators.

Around 17 July 2024 (as reported), in Ciudad Bolivar (Bolivar), CICPC police forces shot and killed an unidentified crime group suspect linked to extortion and theft, during an armed clash in the Tomas de Heres neighborhood, Catedral parish. The suspect resisted authority, initiated a shooting, was injured in the gunfire, and pronounced dead in hospital. An associate of the deceased was arrested in a nearby location. Police seized two guns, two phones, and a vehicle. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 17 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), a group of dentistry students at the Central University of Venezuela (UCV) protested against what they deem as administrative decadence at their school, maltreatment by university teachers, and the lack of medical supplies needed for their dentistry internships. They gathered outside the UCV Dentistry School.

On 17 July 2024, in Ortiz (Guarico), a group of residents and supporters of the Ortiz municipality mayor (VV) protested against his recent impeachment over embezzlement accusations, against the arrest warrant issued for him, and against the appointment of a new PSUV administration in the municipality. Opposition parties argue that this disqualification was politically motivated and that it came after the mayor showed his public support to opposition presidential candidate Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia (PUEDE/MUD), and the disqualified Maria Corina Machado (VV). The protesters gathered outside the Ortiz municipality hall. Police forces were present but there was no intervention.
On 17 July 2024, in Falcon state (coded to Coro), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, education, labor, and political participation.
On 17 July 2024, in Portuguesa state (coded to Guanare), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, education, labor, and political participation.
On 17 July 2024, in La Trinidad de Orichuna (Apure), a group of residents protested over outages in gas for domestic use going on for at least a month.
On 17 July 2024, in Carabobo state (coded to Valencia), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, education, labor, and political participation.

On 16 July 2024, in Maracaibo (Zulia), a group of residents of the Nueva Independencia neighborhood protested over power outages going on for at least a month due to the breakdown of an electric transformer, and to demand solutions from the Corpoelec power company. They argue that this situation negatively impacts their living conditions and livelihoods. They gathered outside the Corpoelec Amparo Office.

On 16 July 2024, in Maturin (Monagas), a group of residents of the Cano Los Becerros village (Monagas), who were affected by the explosion of several gas cylinders back in December 2020, their relatives, and one lawyer, gathered to demand answers on the case, and the expedition of the judicial procedures and investigations to determine the responsibility of local authorities. At least nine people died in that explosion, including three children, and several others were injured. They gathered outside the Monagas state Public Ministry Office.

On 15 July 2024, in Santa Rita (Miranda), members of a local unidentified criminal group associated with the Falcon state Los Chicateros gang shot and killed a fellow gang member, a spotter who's job was to watch out for security forces. It is suspected that the deceased had failed at spotting the CICPC and Falcon state police units that ended killing the four Los Chicateros gang members, including their leader, that morning (coded separately). There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 15 July 2024, in Maturin (Monagas), a group of teachers and other workers at the Antonio Jose de Sucre School, protested to demand the immediate liberation of a fellow teacher, arrested recently under accusations of having harassed three female students. The protesters argue that the three students had repeated grade several times, that they were bad students, that the teacher has had an impeccable career, and that all this was staged in order for them to pass a subject. The demonstrators gathered outside the Public Ministry Office.

On 15 July 2024, in Anzoategui state (coded to Barcelona), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, water, healthcare, political participation, and private property.

On 15 July 2024, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a group of cancer patients, and their relatives, protested to demand the provision of drugs required for their cancer treatments, at subsidized prices, and improvements in staffing and infrastructure at public medical facilities. According to them, the IVSS Alto Costo Social Security pharmacies have not been handing out these medicines in over eight months, but there are other private pharmacies that do sell these products at unaffordable prices. They argue that 2,500 patients are affected by this situation. They gathered outside the Lara state Healthcare Directorate office, where they managed to speak with the Lara state Director of Healthcare.

On 15 July 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), demonstrators protested with unspecified demands on issues related to housing, water, healthcare, political participation, and private property.

On 15 July 2024, in Cumana (Sucre), a small group of residents of the Las Palomas sector blocked the Cacique Maraguey Avenue in protest over power outages going on for at least 17 hours, and to demand solutions from the Corpoelec power company.

On 14 July 2024, in Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), unidentified shooters (likely gang members due to the location) shot and killed a man, in the Yaritagua stairs in the Julian Blanco neighborhood, Petare parish. According to witnesses, the victim was not a resident of the neighborhood; he was dragged there by unidentified armed men who shot him at least 20 times in the face. The authorities suspect the killing is a settling of scores; some witnesses claim that the victim had attended a party the night before, where he was seen having a dispute with several people. 1 fatality.

actor2: Police Forces of Venezuela (1999-) CPNB: National Bolivarian Police
notes: On 13 July 2024, near Araure city (Portuguesa), an on-duty PNB police inspector was shot and killed in the main road of the Guacuy sector. His body was found with a gunshot wound to the head. Nothing was stolen from the crime scene. There is no further information at this point in time. 1 fatality.

On 12 July 2024, in Caracas - Sucre (Miranda), two unidentified crime group suspects opened fire on two Yummy Rides motorcycle delivery drivers, killing one, while they were driving two women to the Maca neighborhood, Petare parish. The victims picked up the women by the Chacao tube station, who requested to be transported to the Petare parish. When they were about to arrive at their destination, one of the women starting talking on the phone, at which point two suspects began to follow them on another motorcycle; shortly after, in the Las Damas sector, the travellers jumped off the Yummy Rides drivers' motorcycles, and one of the suspects opened fire on the riders. One of the victims was killed, the second received medical treatment in hospital. There is no further information on the identity of the perpetrators, or if the women were collaborating with the shooters. Police suspect the killing is a settling of scores. 1 fatality.

On 13 June 2022, in Los Guasimitos (Barinas), residents blocked a bridge over the Santo Domingo river on Trunk Road 5 to protest against electricity blackouts in the area. Demonstrators stated the most recent blackout left their community without power for more than fifteen hours.

Around 27 December 2022 (as reported), in Lander municipality (coded to Ocumare del Tuy, Miranda), suspected members of the Carlos Capa gang held a farmer family of 11 hostage in their farm, in the Los Vegotes sector. The kidnappers demanded a ransom and cattle for their liberation. Two of the captives managed to escape after several days and alert the police. PNB police forces intervened on 4 January to liberate the family after approximately eight days of captivity, although there is no further information on this event at this point in time. There were no arrests.

On 5 January 2023, in Ganango (Carabobo), a vigilante mob of residents attempted to lynch a man that had stabbed another, in the main avenue of the location. Carabobo state police intervened to protect the integrity of the perpetrator. The victim of the stabbing was taken to hospital for treatment. There is no further information on this event at this point in time.
